PyTorch’s GRU returns both per-position outputs and final hidden states. For the supplied left-padded histories, the final nonpadding index is L−1 for nonempty rows; count−1 is incorrect. GRU biases also mean zero-valued padding can change recurrent state, so invariance to adding leading padding requires explicit masking or equivalent handling. Suggested calibration: mixed-length synthetic histories, an independent stepwise reference, and deliberately incorrect count−1/penultimate readouts. Full-length histories alone can miss the indexing fault. [GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html)

PyTorch explicitly warns that batched and individually computed results need not be bitwise identical. Therefore test singleton versus batch, batch permutation, and candidate chunking with fixed evaluation mode and predefined absolute/relative tolerances; record feature errors, score errors, ranking changes and cutoff margins separately. Compare the trained model and generated predictor on identical histories and every candidate score, including partial batches and all four category routes. Check comparison counts and finite values: an empty comparison must never pass. These are proposed applications of the documented numerical caveats. [Numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html)

DeepMutation supports evaluating tests through injected model faults without retraining, although its reported experiments concern image classifiers. A GRU-specific adaptation should inject temporary wrapper faults—wrong readout, cross-user state leakage, candidate-ID permutation, constant scores, skipped chunks—while preserving checkpoint bytes. Report a probe-by-fault detection matrix, valid comparison counts, mutation detection rates and false alarms on unchanged controls. Include deterministic synthetic scoring controls with known expected responses to expose insensitive probes. Freeze thresholds before fault evaluation; surviving mutants indicate coverage gaps or equivalent behavior, rather than grounds to relax thresholds. [DeepMutation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.05206)
